beginner.label: Oil Crisis Despite Reserve Release
beginner.body: <cite index="22-1,25-13">The IEA released 400 million barrels from emergency reserves, its largest release ever, as oil prices spiked due to the Iran war</cite>. <cite index="26-4,26-13">Oil prices briefly fell after the announcement but quickly climbed back above $88 per barrel</cite>. <cite index="25-9">The Strait of Hormuz closure has created the biggest oil supply disruption in history</cite>.

beginner.label: Markets Mixed on Energy Fears
beginner.body: <cite index="7-1">Energy stocks surged 25% year-to-date while tech stocks fell 5%</cite>. <cite index="9-5,9-6">The Dow dropped 308 points while the Nasdaq managed small gains</cite>. <cite index="8-18">Energy companies like Valero and CF Industries led market gains</cite>.

beginner.label: Inflation Stays Calm Before Storm
beginner.body: <cite index="11-10,11-12">February inflation came in exactly at 2.4% as expected, with core prices at 2.5%</cite>. <cite index="11-6,11-9">Economists warned this was 'calm before the storm' as the data predates the recent oil surge</cite>. <cite index="11-5">The Fed will likely keep rates unchanged at its March 18 meeting</cite>.

moderate.label: Oil Crisis Despite Reserve Release
moderate.body: <cite index="22-1,23-3">The IEA approved releasing 400 million barrels from emergency reserves, more than double the 182.7 million released after Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022</cite>. <cite index="26-4,30-8">Despite the announcement, oil prices climbed above $88 per barrel as Brent traded over $90</cite>. <cite index="25-6,25-9">About 20% of global oil normally flows through the Strait of Hormuz, creating the biggest supply disruption in history</cite>. <cite index="30-9,30-10">The release equals just four days of global production, with analysts saying 'it isn't much'</cite>.

moderate.label: Markets Mixed on Energy Fears
moderate.body: <cite index="7-1,7-4">Energy stocks rallied 25% year-to-date as Brent crude jumped from $70 to over $110 per barrel, while tech stocks fell 5%</cite>. <cite index="9-1,9-2,9-7">The Dow fell 308 points to close at 47,398, the S&P 500 dropped to 6,770, but the Nasdaq gained 5.89 points to 22,703</cite>. <cite index="7-11,7-12">Resource giants like ExxonMobil and Chevron benefited from higher crude prices and increased production quotas</cite>. <cite index="7-14">Copper hit $6.11 per pound due to massive data center wiring requirements</cite>.

moderate.label: Inflation Stays Calm Before Storm
moderate.body: <cite index="11-10,11-12,18-4">February CPI rose 0.3% monthly and 2.4% annually, matching forecasts exactly, with core inflation at 2.5%</cite>. <cite index="11-6,11-7,11-8">Economists warned this was the 'calm before the storm' as tariff impacts hit core goods while services inflation remained hot</cite>. <cite index="11-9,20-32">The data predates the oil surge from the Iran war, so energy impacts will appear in March data</cite>. <cite index="11-5,20-38">The Fed will likely hold rates steady at 3.5%-3.75% through its next three meetings</cite>.

expert.label: Oil Crisis Despite Reserve Release
expert.body: <cite index="22-1,23-3,24-5">The IEA's unanimous approval of a 400 million barrel emergency release dwarfs the 182.7 million barrel response to Russia's Ukraine invasion, yet markets remain skeptical</cite>. <cite index="26-4,26-13,30-8">WTI crude briefly dipped below session lows after the announcement before climbing back above $88, with Brent trading over $90</cite>. <cite index="29-6,29-8">Export volumes through the Strait of Hormuz have collapsed to less than 10% of pre-conflict levels, disrupting 20 million barrels per day that normally transit the waterway</cite>. <cite index="26-19,28-17">JPMorgan notes that U.S. SPR releases typically take 13 days to begin delivery, while physical flow limits constrain how quickly stockpiles can be emptied</cite>. <cite index="30-9,28-19">The release equals just four days of global production and cannot substitute for restoring Strait access, according to analysts</cite>.

expert.label: Markets Mixed on Energy Fears
expert.body: <cite index="7-1,7-2,7-4">The energy sector's 25% YTD rally versus tech's 5% decline reflects a dramatic escalation that sent Brent from $70 in late 2025 to over $110 by mid-March</cite>. <cite index="9-1,9-2,9-7">The Dow's 308-point decline (-0.65%) to 47,398 contrasted with the Nasdaq's modest 5.89-point gain (+0.03%) to 22,703 on semiconductor strength</cite>. <cite index="7-7,7-8,7-9">The 'AI Power Wall' has emerged as data center electricity demand outpaces green energy supply, forcing a return to fossil fuels and nuclear</cite>. <cite index="7-12,7-14">ExxonMobil and Chevron benefited from higher quotas and crude prices, while copper reached $6.11/pound on data center infrastructure demand</cite>. <cite index="10-4,10-10">BlackRock warns of market complacency with limited directional equity exposure and reduced U.S. equity positioning given AI deployment concentration risks</cite>.

expert.label: Inflation Stays Calm Before Storm
expert.body: <cite index="11-10,11-12,18-7,18-10">February's 0.3% monthly CPI gain and 2.4% annual rate matched consensus precisely, with core CPI at 0.2% monthly and 2.5% annually, near 2021 lows</cite>. <cite index="11-6,11-7,11-8">The Carson Group's Varghese characterized this as 'calm before the storm,' noting tariff impacts on core goods and persistent services inflation outside housing</cite>. <cite index="18-8,18-9,20-35">Shelter contributed the largest monthly increase at 0.2%, while gasoline rose 0.8% and food gained 0.4%</cite>. <cite index="11-9,20-32,8-8">The data predates the Iran conflict oil shock, with the EU warning inflation could exceed 3% if Brent sustains $100/barrel levels</cite>. <cite index="11-5,2-2,20-38">Fed funds futures price a March hold at 3.5%-3.75% with near-100% odds, as the FOMC maintains data-dependent policy amid divisions on easing pace</cite>.
